toc.title: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew (skill 3.4.2)

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. ETL: extract, transform, load; DLQ: dead-letter queue; DMS: Database Migration Service; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; DPU: data processing unit; CDC: change data capture; GSI: global secondary index; AQE: adaptive query execution

  • Run data quality checks while processing data (for example empty fields)
  • Define data quality rules with AWS Glue DataBrew (and AWS Glue Data Quality)
  • Investigate data consistency
  • Describe data sampling techniques
  • Implement mechanisms for data skew

2Dimensions of Data Quality

Running case

Kestrel Freight Trusts Its Numbers

  • An invoice run billed a customer twice because of duplicate orders
  • Some trucks report temperature as −999 and some weights as zero
  • Yesterday's file was half the usual size and nobody noticed
  • Your job: catch bad data before it reaches reports
Dimension Question Example check
Completeness Is anything missing? shipment_id is never null; at least 95% of customer_id filled
Uniqueness Are there duplicates? shipment_id unique
Validity Does it fit the allowed format, type or range? Weight between 0 and 40,000 kg; date format; allowed status values
Accuracy Does it match reality? Delivered count equals the count in the source system
Consistency Do related values agree across fields, tables or systems? Delivery date is not before pickup date; source and target totals match
Timeliness (freshness) Is it recent enough? Latest record is less than 2 hours old
Integrity Do references resolve? Every customer_id exists in the customer table
Volume Is the amount normal? Row count within ±20% of the usual
Exam tip

Match the problem to the dimension: nulls → completeness, duplicates → uniqueness, out-of-range → validity, source ≠ target → consistency, late data → timeliness.

3Running Checks While Processing (skill 3.4.1)

  • Check early and during processing, not only at the end: at ingestion, after each transformation, and before publishing
  • Where to run checks:
Where How
AWS Glue ETL jobs AWS Glue Data Quality (the EvaluateDataQuality transform with a ruleset) or Spark code (filter, counts, null checks)
AWS Glue Data Catalog tables Glue Data Quality rulesets run on a schedule or on demand against a table
AWS Glue DataBrew Rulesets and profile jobs (visual)
AWS Lambda Small, event-driven validation of an arriving file
Athena / Redshift SQL Set-based checks (COUNT, WHERE col IS NULL, GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
Streaming Flink or Lambda validate records; bad records go to a dead-letter destination
  • What to do with a failure (choose by severity):
    • Fail the job and alert (a critical rule broke)
    • Quarantine the bad records to a rejected S3 prefix or DLQ with the reason, and continue with the good ones
    • Fix automatically (default values, standardization) and log the change
    • Alert only (a warning rule)
  • Examples of checks: empty fields, schema match, data types, ranges, uniqueness, referential integrity, row counts, freshness

AWS Glue Data Quality

  • Define rules in DQDL (Data Quality Definition Language), evaluate them in ETL jobs or on catalog tables, get a quality score and rule-by-rule results (to the console, S3, CloudWatch and EventBridge)
  • Built on the open-source Deequ; Glue can recommend rules from the data
Rules = [
    IsComplete "shipment_id",
    Uniqueness "shipment_id" > 0.99,
    ColumnValues "weight_kg" between 0 and 40000,
    ColumnValues "status" in ["PICKED","IN_TRANSIT","DELIVERED"],
    RowCount > 1000
]
Exam tip

"Stop the job or route bad rows to a quarantine when required fields are empty" → Glue Data Quality rules in the job, with bad records written to a rejected location and an alert.

4Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew (skill 3.4.2)

  • AWS Glue DataBrew profiles data and applies data quality rules without code
  • Profile job: computes statistics per column: missing values, distinct count, duplicates, min, max, mean, distribution, correlations, outliers
  • Ruleset: a named set of rules attached to a dataset; each rule has checks (conditions on a column or the whole dataset), thresholds (for example fail if more than 5% missing) and a severity
  • Typical checks: column is not null, values within a range or list, column value matches a pattern, uniqueness, row count, column statistics, data type
  • Validation results (pass or fail per rule) are written to S3, and a failed ruleset can stop or alert the pipeline; run on a schedule
  • Pick the tool: DataBrew for visual, analyst-owned rules; Glue Data Quality (DQDL) for engineer-owned rules inside jobs and catalogs

5Investigating Data Consistency (skill 3.4.3)

  • Consistency means the same facts agree across fields, records, tables and systems, and over time
  • Investigate with:
    • Profiling (DataBrew profile job): duplicates, missing values, correlations, odd distributions
    • Reconciliation queries: compare counts, sums, min and max (or hashes) between source and target
    • Cross-field rules: delivered_date >= pickup_date; totals equal the sum of lines
    • Referential checks: orphan keys with a left join
    • Glue Data Quality dataset checks: compare two datasets
    • AWS DMS data validation: compares rows in source and target after a migration or replication and reports mismatches
  • System-level consistency to know:
    • Amazon S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for object writes, overwrites and deletes and for listings
    • DynamoDB: reads are eventually consistent by default; request a strongly consistent read when you must see the latest write (not available on global secondary indexes); transactions give all-or-nothing writes
    • Distributed pipelines: at-least-once delivery causes duplicates, so idempotent writes and de-duplication keep data consistent
    • Apache Iceberg and transactions give atomic commits to lake tables
  • Fixing inconsistency: find the source of truth, correct upstream, reprocess (idempotently), add a rule so it is caught next time
Exam tip

"After migrating, prove source and target match" → AWS DMS data validation (plus row-count and checksum comparisons).

6Data Sampling Techniques (skill 3.4.4)

  • Sampling takes a subset of data to profile, test or check it quickly and cheaply instead of scanning everything
  • Techniques:
Technique How Use it when
Simple random Every row has equal chance General profiling; avoids bias
Systematic Every n-th row Ordered data, fast and simple (watch for hidden patterns)
Stratified Sample within each group (route, region) in proportion Rare groups must be represented
Cluster Pick whole groups (a partition or file) at random Cheap when reading whole files
Reservoir Keep a fixed-size random sample of a stream of unknown length Streaming data
First-N (head) Take the first rows Quick look only: may be biased
  • In AWS: DataBrew profile jobs can use the full dataset or a sample (for example the first N rows or a random N rows); Athena TABLESAMPLE and Spark sample() for random subsets; Glue Data Quality and Spark jobs can run on a sample to save cost
  • Cautions: a sample can miss rare errors and can be biased; use bigger or stratified samples for rare events and run full checks for critical rules

7Data Skew (skill 3.4.5)

  • Data skew = values are not evenly spread: one key holds a large share of the rows, so one partition, node, shard or task does most of the work (a straggler) or runs out of memory
  • Symptoms: one task much slower in the Spark UI; one Kinesis shard or DynamoDB partition throttled while others idle; one Redshift slice holds many more rows; out-of-memory on one executor
  • Mechanisms to handle skew:
Where Fix
Spark (Glue, EMR) Salting: add a random suffix to the hot key, aggregate in two steps; repartition on a better key; broadcast the small side of a join; enable adaptive query execution skew-join handling; filter hot or null keys and process them separately
Redshift Choose a distribution key with many distinct, evenly used values; use EVEN or AUTO; check skew in table information views; avoid a key with many nulls
DynamoDB High-cardinality partition key, or a suffix (write sharding) for very hot keys; spread keys
Kinesis / Kafka Partition key with many values; add a random suffix for hot keys; split the hot shard or use on-demand
S3 / Athena Partition by a balanced column; avoid a few giant partitions; compact small files
Exam tip

"One task runs for hours while the rest finish in seconds after a join on customer_id, and one customer has most rows" → data skew: salt the key, broadcast, or enable adaptive skew handling.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1During an AWS Glue job the team must stop processing and alert when required fields such as shipment_id are empty, and route other invalid records for review. What is the best design?

  • AIgnore the null values in the job and fix the data next month
  • BGlue Data Quality rules in the job, bad records written to a rejected S3 prefix, and an alert on failure
  • CConvert all the input files to CSV before the job reads them
  • DIncrease the number of DPUs so that the job finishes before checks
Show the answer

Answer: B. Quality rules in the job detect problems early, quarantining isolates bad records with the reason, and alerts notify the team.

S2Analysts without coding skills want to define data quality checks such as "no more than 5% missing values in the weight column" and review pass or fail results. Which service should they use?

  • AAWS Glue DataBrew rulesets and profile jobs
  • BAmazon Kinesis Data Streams with a validating consumer
  • CAWS CloudTrail trails with data events turned on
  • DAmazon Macie jobs that scan the files for personal data
Show the answer

Answer: A. DataBrew provides visual data quality rules with thresholds and validation results without code.

S3After a database migration the team must confirm that the rows in the target match the source. Which TWO actions help? (Select TWO.)

  • ADelete the source before checking
  • BCompare row counts and checksums between source and target
  • CIncrease the replication instance size only
  • DEnable AWS DMS data validation on the task
  • EDisable CDC
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. DMS data validation compares source and target rows, and count and checksum comparisons confirm consistency. The other actions do not verify data.

S4A join on customer_id makes one Spark task run for hours because a single customer has most of the rows. Which TWO actions reduce the problem? (Select TWO.)

  • AWrite the output as many more small files
  • BTurn off partitioning of the input
  • CRemove the join and keep both tables unsorted
  • DEnable adaptive query execution skew-join handling
  • ESalt the hot key and aggregate in two steps
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Uneven key distribution is data skew; salting the hot key and adaptive skew-join handling spread the work across tasks. Small files, no partitioning and dropping the join do not fix the imbalance.

S5A team wants to profile a very large dataset quickly and cheaply and make sure rare categories are represented. Which sampling technique is best?

  • ATake the first 1,000 rows
  • BStratified sampling within each category
  • CTake every row
  • DSystematic sampling of every 1,000,000th row
Show the answer

Answer: B. Stratified sampling samples within each group, so rare categories are represented; the first rows can be biased.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Dimensions Completeness, uniqueness, validity, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, integrity, volume
Checks in processing Early and repeated; Glue Data Quality (DQDL) in jobs and on catalog tables, DataBrew rulesets, Lambda, SQL; fail, quarantine, fix or warn
DQDL Rules = [ IsComplete "col", Uniqueness "col" > 0.99, ColumnValues "col" between a and b, RowCount > n ]; built on Deequ; score and results to S3/CloudWatch/EventBridge
DataBrew Profile job (missing, duplicates, distribution, outliers), ruleset with checks, thresholds, severity, validation results in S3
Consistency Profile, reconcile counts/sums/hashes, cross-field and referential rules, DMS data validation; S3 strong consistency; DynamoDB strongly consistent reads (not on GSIs); idempotent writes
Sampling Random, systematic, stratified, cluster, reservoir (streams), first-N (biased); Athena TABLESAMPLE, Spark sample(); samples can miss rare errors
Skew One hot key → straggler; salting, repartition, broadcast, AQE skew join, better Redshift dist key, DynamoDB/Kinesis key suffix, balanced S3 partitions
